t: Section 3(a)(4) of the Securities Act of 1933 (15 U.S.C. 77c(a)(4)) is amended by inserting after the semicolon at the end the following: “or any security of a fund that is excluded from the definition of an investment company under section 3(c)(10)(B) of the Investment Company Act of 1940;”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Securities Act of 1933 to add an exempted class of securities (those of funds excluded from the investment company definition). It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No tempting reading exists beyond the mention of a 'fund', which is a regulated entity and not a participant in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only amends the definition of exempt securities in Section 3(a)(4) of the Securities Act. It adds securities of funds excluded under section 3(c)(10)(B) of the Investment Company Act. It sets up no public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. Reading it as participation just because it touches securities regulation is wrong, because nothing in the text brings outside parties into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statutory definition regarding securities law exemptions. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. It is a substantive change to the law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3(a)(4) of the Securities Act of 1933 (15 U.S.C. 77c(a)(4)) is amended by inserting after the semicolon at the end the following: “or any security of a fund that is excluded from the definition of an investment company under section 3(c)(10)(B) of the Investment Company Act of 1940;”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the definition of an investment company affects who can participate in securities offerings, but the text itself is purely definitional and regulatory. It does not establish a process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input. It simply changes the scope of a statutory exemption.
